title: The Silent Grave
subtitle: They've gone—to the depths of the sea.

items.text: The Sea Breeze Still Whispers
The Silent Grave
Nukutaeao
Waves lap gently at the reef, just as they always have, washing over the pristine white sands.
As the sun sets, plumes of smoke rise from the cozy homes of the islanders. The glowing Sea Mother's Eye lanterns hang high above, shimmering in the dusk, all pointing the way back home.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Fatutu, let's do one final check on the canoes. We don't want Toa tipping into the sea during tomorrow's race.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Toa's been rattling with excitement for days. If he falls in, I doubt it'll be the canoe's fault.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Besides, brother, you'll be the one that has to dive in after him!

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: He swims a lot faster than I do.
The canoes are neatly lined up on the beach, each showing different degrees of wear.
Painted and adorned by various Nukutai hands, they stand like a row of strange, silent gravestones.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We haven't made a new canoe in a long time.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: These old ones are enough to carry all the young folks of Nukutaeao. Paddle out to Itiiti, circle around to Miti and Vaipuna, then come back to Meli ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Not if you count me! By next year, I'll be old enough to paddle too!
Hearing the faint mix of complaint and anticipation in his sister's voice, Kamuta falls silent for a moment as the sea breeze stirs around them.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Fatutu, for next year's canoe race around the island, I'll build you a new boat. How about that?

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: We'll find a tree with the straightest trunk, shape the prow just right. When the wind and waves come, you'll ride them like they're part of you.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Kamuta ...

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Fatutu will have her own canoe, one that no one can catch, because she'll be the fastest on the water.
He paints a shining vision of a new canoe. But behind him, a wave looms silently above them, as tall as a mountain, like a curtain of black.
And it falls.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Fatu ... tu ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Brother ... Toa ... Where are you? Where did you go?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Wait for me! I'm coming!
The sea rises and falls, and the girl's thin voice fades under the rush of waves.
But no one answers.
The water wraps around her with familiar weight. And Fatutu knows exactly where it's carrying her.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I want to go home. I've been gone too long. Brother, Toa, are you gone now?
Fatutu floats through the open sea, eyes straining toward the horizon where ocean meets sky—unbroken, unending.
Her island has sunk beneath the waves.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Gone ... it's all gone ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Gone ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Miti, Vaipuna, Meli ... our islands ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I shouldn't have left. Why did I leave?
Her question is swallowed up like a drop lost in the ocean—without ripples, without reply.
Fatutu!
Wake up, wake up! Fatutu!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Selone?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Kamuta ...
Realizing the nightmare is over, Fatutu immediately shuts her mouth.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: That was another bad dream, wasn't it?
Fatutu looks for words but only nods.
Selone lifts her shell necklace, placing one shell gently against Fatutu's forehead.
Fatutu lifts her own in reply and presses it to Selone's brow.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: "Swept into the tide, scattered by the wind, gone into the mist."

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: "Let the siren's song not lead me astray; let nightmare's voice not steal me from my home."

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: "The shell's warning keeps me on course. Its grooves show me the path."

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: "I will return. I have returned."

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: You taught me that song, remember?
Selone's words pull Fatutu out from the cold sea of her nightmare at last.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: That was the day you and Toa snuck out to sea and got caught in the storm, right?

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I wanted to pick Compassare from Itiiti that day—just one more sprig for my Sea Mother's Eye. I didn't listen to the shell's guidance, and I talked Toa into taking me.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Our canoe had barely left the shore, but the wind suddenly swept us out to sea. Toa paddled with everything he had, clutching that Compassare the whole time.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Brother was holding back tears when he realized you were gone; he was so worried. Remember how you and Toa got such a scolding?

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: For a long while after, I was terrified, afraid that making it back had just been a dream, afraid that maybe the ocean had taken Toa after all.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: So you sang to me.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I will return. I have returned.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Selone ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: How are you doing now? I mean, since we came here, we don't ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Live as closely as we used to.
It's not an easy question to answer.
Before offering each other comfort, the two friends begin to feel how small their tribe is now, and how fragile.
Selone's tears fall hot on Fatutu's arm, cooling over her tan skin.
Fatutu pulls her in tightly. Their shell necklaces knock together with a soft sound.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I'm sorry, Fatutu.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: At least it's nice here. I've learned to write their language. I've been to their library. I've learned so much about the outside world.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: But it's nothing like what we imagined. We believed in those stories so much that we never thought to understand what was really out there.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: We never thought we'd leave ...

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Even when we knew how it would all end.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I miss Toa. I miss Kamuta. I miss our island, our home ...
Slow rivers of tears carve across Fatutu's skin, sharp with grief.
She pats Selone's back; she can do nothing else. Trying to hold back their shared sorrow is like standing against a falling wave.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I'm here, Selone.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We won't lose each other again.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Brother and Toa have already reached where they're meant to be. Their souls rest in the depths of the sea; they aren't truly lost.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: They'll always be there to watch over us.
Is that true?
They feel hollow, like she's not sure what to believe anymore, but they feel like the right words to say to keep her friend and her afloat.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Our home—our island—it will survive as long as we do.
The Hall in the Suitcase
Sonetto stops quietly, a paper form in her hand signed with small, careful writing.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, Miss Fatutu has submitted a request. She ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: She's asking for a form of arcane skill that can put her into a peaceful sleep, or, if not possible, then any medicine that might help.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Medicine?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: She's been plagued by nightmares. She didn't explain what they were about. Perhaps she didn't want to relive them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I can understand her pain. Did she say anything else?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: No, Timekeeper. She passed the form to me and left without a word.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I must note that Miss Fatutu's request was written exceptionally well. By the book, really. Not many people manage to be that precise.
The Foundation's forms are painfully tedious. It's nothing short of remarkable that Fatutu managed to navigate through them herself.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll see what I can do to streamline the application and approval process for everyone in the suitcase. We don't need to be burdened with this kind of unnecessary paperwork.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: As for our friend, Fatutu, if she wants to rid herself of memories she no longer wants to revisit, then I think there might be a better way than arcane skill or medication.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But it'll take time.
